Outcome_variable.extract_value: life satisfaction, positive affect, negative affect
Outcome_variable.evidence_source: [/page/20/Text/5] That higher versus lower levels of positive functioning were predicted over time, respectively, by high SWB versus low SWB configurations (and movements toward these configurations) in both the categorical cluster membership and prototypicality score approaches is consonant with Shmotkin's (2005) proposal concerning the ''double-edged sword'' (p. 309) of congruous SWB profiles. From this perspective, congruity may be personally advantageous due to complementarity among components when configured as a high SWB profile, but debilitating when low levels of LS and PA coincide with high NA. [/page/21/Text/3] Rather, the capacity for extracting satisfaction in one's life and avoiding negative emotions may have enabled successful adaptation to emotionally complex situations and life challenges, including those related to relatively infrequent positive affective experiences (Shmotkin et al. 2006). Thus, compensation among SWB components resulting from a particularly favorable (low) level of NA in combination with moderate levels of LS and PA might have aided in promoting healthy functioning—and may have been just as effective at doing so as a high SWB profile.
